items.title: Handle non-blocking stdio and retry on EAGAIN in printer
items.reason: Opened specifically to fix astral-sh/uv#22170 by retrying WouldBlock writes. It was closed unmerged after review questioned supporting inherited O_NONBLOCK and identified Bun as the likely source; it is not a duplicate basis.

items.title: uv panics when resizing terminal window
items.reason: An adjacent output-write panic where a closed stdout pipe produces EPIPE/BrokenPipe during completion generation. It differs from the new printer stderr EAGAIN failure.

items.title: fix: handle BrokenPipe in shell completion generation
items.reason: Proposes explicit BrokenPipe handling for astral-sh/uv#12244, but does not handle WouldBlock in the shared printer.

items.title: Race condition in SIGPIPE causes network errors to kill uv run
items.reason: Concerns EPIPE/SIGPIPE from a uv-owned write being forwarded to a child. It is related to pipe failure handling but differs from the double-panic SIGABRT caused by stderr EAGAIN.

related.search_scope: Literal searches covered EAGAIN, "Resource temporarily unavailable", "failed printing to stderr", O_NONBLOCK, WouldBlock, SIGABRT, socketpair, non-blocking stderr, and printer.rs. Conceptual and fix-oriented searches covered output-write panics, pipe backpressure, child-process stdio, BrokenPipe/EPIPE, SIGPIPE, retrying writes, and printer fixes across open and closed issues and open, closed, and merged pull requests. astral-sh/uv#21337 was ruled out because its subprocess SIGABRT was traced to workspace discovery. astral-sh/uv#3150 and astral-sh/uv#14462 were ruled out because their similar error text came from Rayon thread-pool creation. No pre-existing tracker covers this exact stderr EAGAIN failure.

type_reason: The blocking/non-blocking comparison and syscall trace establish that a transient stderr EAGAIN reaches printer.rs, triggers a panic, and causes a second failed panic write followed by SIGABRT. The checked-in printer still delegates to print macros at that location. Although inherited O_NONBLOCK may originate in the parent runtime—and Bun merged oven-sh/bun#43868 to clear it for spawned children—the demonstrated abort remains incorrect behavior. This is not a duplicate because astral-sh/uv#22195 was opened in response to this report and closed unmerged.
summary: No earlier issue tracks the exact failure. The closest item is the closed, unmerged response PR astral-sh/uv#22195; the other items cover distinct BrokenPipe or SIGPIPE paths. The issue-context README remains unchanged because the active read-only filesystem sandbox rejected the required write.
draft_response: Thanks for the detailed reproduction. The syscall trace and current printer implementation confirm that a transient EAGAIN from stderr reaches the print path, which panics; the panic hook then tries the same full stream and the process aborts. astral-sh/uv#22195 proposed retrying these writes, but it was closed unmerged because inherited O_NONBLOCK was viewed as a caller-side stdio problem. For Bun specifically, oven-sh/bun#43868 now clears O_NONBLOCK for spawned children; Node's spawn already gives children blocking stdio. Could you share the exact Bun spawn code and confirm whether this still reproduces with a Bun build containing oven-sh/bun#43868? The standalone Python reproduction remains useful for deciding whether uv should also handle EAGAIN defensively.
